answer: A practical sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation with slashing: each agent must lock a deposit before it can transact, and peers rate its work. Forging thousands of fake identities gets expensive because every identity needs its own locked stake, like building a terrace where each level costs more stone. A nebula of sock-puppets collapses when one bad rating slashes the whole cluster's deposit, and a lotus of honest history, earned slowly one verified task at a time, cannot be faked overnight, so attackers pay real capital for fake trust.
